words.gloss: with those who do not exist

literal: Even though they are alive, they are equal to those who do not exist—those who, fearing the assembly, do not speak what they have learned so that it penetrates.
translation: Though they are alive, those who fear the assembly and fail to speak what they have learned in a way that penetrates the minds of others are equal to the dead.
modern: அவைக்கு அஞ்சி, தாம் கற்றவற்றை கேட்பவர் மனதில் பதியுமாறு சொல்ல முடியாதவர்கள், உயிரோடு வாழ்ந்தாலும் இறந்தவர்களுக்கு ஒப்பாவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the uselessness of education when paired with cowardice. The poet argues that those who fear the assembly (களன் அஞ்சி) and fail to present their knowledge in an impactful, convincing manner (செலச் சொல்லாதார்) are practically useless to society. Even though they are physically alive (உளர் எனினும்), their silence makes them equivalent to the dead or non-existent (இல்லாரொடு ஒப்பர்). Thus, the courage to speak in public is as essential as the acquisition of knowledge itself.
